nodes.description: In a rare hereditary, X-linked dominant ovarian immature teratoma—distinct from benign mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst), for which no causal germline variant has been demonstrated—a germline BMP15 missense mutation (C262T; p.Arg88Cys) reduces secretion of mature BMP15 by ~85%. Loss of BMP15 oocyte growth-factor signaling is associated with abnormal activation of the H-Ras/MAPK pathway in oocytes, which markedly increases spontaneous parthenogenetic oocyte activation and predisposes to ovarian immature teratoma formation. Included here because it defines a molecular route to spontaneous oocyte parthenogenesis in human ovarian teratoma biology.

nodes.description: Ovarian mature cystic teratoma originates from an ovarian germ cell/oocyte that develops parthenogenetically (without fertilization), classically after completion of meiosis I. Ovarian teratomas typically have a normal karyotype and exhibit maternal-pattern genomic imprinting—reduced methylation at paternally methylated loci and increased methylation at maternally methylated loci—distinguishing them from malignant ovarian germ cell tumors such as dysgerminomas and yolk-sac tumors that frequently harbor chromosome 12p gains. The post-meiosis-I parthenogenetic model is not settled: a small Taiwanese genotyping series found heterozygous STR profiles in mature cystic teratomas and proposed an origin from oogonia or primary oocytes before meiosis I instead.

nodes.description: Complete surgical excision is the definitive treatment across all dermoid cyst subtypes. For ovarian dermoid cysts, fertility-sparing cystectomy or oophorectomy is performed, commonly via laparoscopy. Intracranial lesions require neurosurgical resection (gross total resection minimizes recurrence); nasal dermoid sinus cysts require complete excision of the cyst and tract. Completeness of resection is the primary determinant of recurrence.
